title: Budget the bytes and the blocking state
description: Change the source layout, projection, predicate, operator, and memory budget. The model exposes why a selective result can still require a broad scan or a spill.

sources.label: Ordered Parquet
sources.detail: Compressed columns with row groups ordered on the common filter key.
sources.sourceNote: The teaching model assumes physical Parquet bytes are 35% of logical values.

sources.label: Scattered Parquet
sources.detail: Compressed columns, but matching values appear across almost every row group.
sources.sourceNote: Projection still helps, but the modeled predicate cannot skip row groups.

sources.label: CSV files
sources.detail: Row-oriented text requires a broad byte scan and parsing before typed operators run.
sources.sourceNote: The model uses the logical dataset size as the CSV byte baseline.

sources.label: DuckDB table
sources.detail: Persistent columnar storage with compression and zonemap metadata.
sources.sourceNote: The model assumes physical table bytes are 45% of logical values.

filters.label: No filter
filters.detail: Every row contributes to the operator.

filters.label: 2% match, scattered
filters.detail: Few rows match, but those values are distributed across all row groups.

filters.label: 2% clustered range
filters.detail: The source is ordered on the predicate key, so useful metadata can skip most row groups.

operators.label: Filter and project
operators.detail: Rows can flow to the result without retaining the complete input.

operators.label: High-cardinality GROUP BY
operators.detail: Group state grows with distinct keys and may spill when the state exceeds memory.

operators.label: Global ORDER BY
operators.detail: The selected rows must participate in a blocking sort before the final order is known.

operators.label: Many-to-many JOIN
operators.detail: Join output can exceed both inputs when key multiplicity is not bounded.

notice: This is an arithmetic teaching model, not a DuckDB benchmark. Compression, row-group pruning, join cardinality, cache state, and spill behavior must be measured with the real plan and files.
